points.description: Child's kernel context/stack is set up in advance (by fork/allocproc) so that when first scheduled it starts executing in a kernel function (e.g., forkret) rather than via a real trap.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says the child's kernel stack/context is prepared artificially, without saying how it begins executing.

points.description: The kernel stack's return address is set to the trap handler's return path (e.g., trapret), so the function returns into it, emulating a return from a trap, then unwinds the kernel stack to return to user mode.
points.partial_credit: Half if says it fakes/emulates a trap return but does not mention the return address or trap-return code.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying the child's kernel stack/context is prepared so it starts in a function and returns into the trap-return path, imitating a trap return. Give part marks for a vague but right-track answer, e.g. only that the stack is faked to look like a trap. No marks for answers saying a real trap occurs in the child or that are unrelated. Function names (forkret, trapret) are not required.
